title: Consumer Impact Scoring and Migration CLI for Runtime Evolution
creator: Leah Morgan
description:
Summary: Define and implement a reproducible runtime semantic versioning policy that centers on a consumer-impact scoring rubric and a developer-facing migration CLI. The goal is to reduce surprise-breaking changes, standardize deprecation windows per impact tier, and provide automated, reversible migration helpers for customers across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.

Scope: This ticket covers: (1) a documented consumer-impact scorecard (low/med/high with measurable signals), (2) formalized change windows for LTS and non-LTS branches, (3) rollout gate definitions (canary, progressive %, region/tenant filters, auto-fallback), and (4) a migration CLI (amcli-like) that produces client-side adapters, deprecation notices, and optional automated transformation patches. It does not cover kernel-level codegen optimizations or internal-only protocol changes that do not affect external contracts.

Policy highlights: 
- Semver mapping: patch = bugfix/no-contract-change; minor = additive API or opt-in features; major = contract-breaking changes.
- Consumer-impact scoring: changes are scored 0-10 based on telemetry signals (endpoint usage %, typical token length, number of customers using variant), contract exposure (public SDKs vs internal flag), and security implications. Scores map to deprecation windows: 0-2 -> 7 days; 3-5 -> 30 days; 6-8 -> 90 days + migration assist; 9-10 -> require major version and 180-day transition.
- LTS channels: LTS branches accept backported bug/compatibility fixes and additive non-breaking minors; breaking changes must land on next major with a migration plan. Each LTS releases a compatibility advisory with a migration checklist.
- Rollout gates: every change must declare a Gate Plan: canary (>=1%), staged rollout steps (10/30/60/100), metrics to watch (error rate, latency P95, model divergence), auto-rollback thresholds, and fallback model/policy when capacity or regressions detected.

Migration CLI (migration-helper): 
- Functionality: analyzes a repo’s client calls to the runtime API (using OpenAPI + SDK call traces), emits a report of impacted endpoints, generates a best-effort adapter shim, and can produce codemod patches for SDKs (TypeScript, Python, Go).
- Modes: dry-run report, patch suggestion (codemod), and reversible transformation with changelog entry.
- Distribution: shipped as part of the redwoodctl toolbelt and as a standalone pip/npm package for customer use in Private deployments.

Operational and testing requirements: 
- Compatibility test suites: add golden-suite cases that exercise both old and new shapes; include fuzz inputs derived from production traces (sanitized).
- Telemetry gating: require pre-rollout baseline and drift windows; collect contract-usage histograms and surface via Console per-route.
- Canary automation: integrate with rollout automation to run canaries against a representative tenant set for at least 3 hours with defined SLI thresholds before progressing.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Consumer-impact scoring doc published in Confluence with examples and scoring formula.
2) Migration CLI MVP able to generate reports and TypeScript codemod patches for a sample repo (internal reference app).
3) A release checklist template for LTS and non-LTS changes added to the repo (PR template + CI checks).
4) Rollout Gate Plan form added to PR schema and validated by presubmit.

Risks & tradeoffs: 
- Scoring model relies on telemetry quality; noisy signals could misclassify impact. To mitigate, bootstrap with conservative thresholds and manual review for high-impact scores.
- Automated codemods are best-effort and can introduce bugs; require opt-in and reversible patches, and encourage customers to run dry-run.
- Shipping migration tooling increases maintenance surface; prioritize SDKs with highest adoption first.

Links & artifacts: 
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Semver+Scoring+Draft (internal)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2451 (migration-cli prototype)
- Draft CLI package: https://npmjs.com/package/@redwood/migration-helper (private beta)

Next steps: 
- Finish scoring formula and examples (Asha + Marco) by 2026-02-05.
- Merge migration CLI MVP behind feature flag and run internal migration on ref-app by 2026-02-28.
- Run cross-team review (SDK leads, Console, Security) and iterate before rolling out scoring thresholds to canary stage.
